exposure: time period (pre- vs. postimplementation of 2014 guidelines)
cohort: 4,976 term patients who underwent a CD for an arrest disorder between January 2011 and April 2017 at a county teaching hospital
finding: Despite significant changes in labor management after the publication of the 2014 guidelines, the primary CD rate was not reduced, and there was an increase in CMM in patients who had CD for arrest of descent.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of CD for arrest of dilation between the pre- and post-guideline periods, but the rate of CMM significantly increased in patients who had CD for arrest of descent after the implementation of the guidelines.
